result.title: Vision: "What Don't I Know About User's Preferences?" How Uncertainty Estimation Improves Proactive Assistant Alignment
result.comment: Published in Companion of the 2026 ACM International Joint Conference on Pervasive and Ubiquitous Computing (UbiComp Companion '26) PEACE Workshop
result.summary: Proactive Smart Assistants (PSAs) increasingly use general knowledge, learned patterns from group-level data, patterns from individual user's data, and recent sensor observations to anticipate which action a user may prefer. Existing systems typically select actions from predicted user preference likelihoods, but these likelihoods alone do not reveal how reliable the prediction is, which evidence supports it, or why ambiguity remains. In this vision paper, we argue that uncertainty estimation can provide this missing information and substantially change appropriate downstream behavior. Using the example of a home assistant, we introduce the questions that uncertainty estimation aims to answer, i.e. how sure is the assistant about the predicted preference likelihood, whether the confidence come from group-level assumptions or individual's data, and whether likelihood ambiguity reflect the user's intrinsic preference variability or insufficient data for the particular situation. We further introduce uncertainty estimation applications in neighboring domains, such as human trajectory prediction, personalized activity recognition, information-collection, and model-based control. Finally, we draw on insights from neighboring domains to envision how future uncertainty-aware proactive assistants may address key challenges in proactive interaction.

AI.brief_summary: 这篇 vision 论文主张为用户偏好预测补充不确定性估计，以说明预测可靠程度、置信来源（群体先验还是个体数据）以及歧义究竟来自用户内在偏好变化还是数据不足，并借鉴轨迹预测、个性化活动识别、信息采集与基于模型的控制等邻近领域，设想不确定性感知的主动助手。
AI.relevance_reason: 其把不确定性拆成「证据来源」与「歧义成因」的思路，可能与 LVR 中 STOP 决策、证据充分性判断和视觉证据筛选存在概念联系，可供核查，但论文面向普适计算而非多模态推理，属远领域启发。
